name: Talk Dirty Dance AI: Lead the Concert Dance Break From One Photo
blurb: The Talk Dirty dance trend is a fan's phone video of the dance break of "Talk Dirty" at a concert, with a new face on the lead dancer.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 15 s, 720p, 9:16, sound off. The video prompt
prompts.text:
Recreate the reference video [Video 1] shot for shot: the same fan's phone video from the crowd of a concert dance break on a big stage, a line of backup dancers in yellow-and-black and red-and-black jackets, flame columns, white spotlights and a large LED wall, with the same handheld camera, zooms, framing, timing and moves. The ONLY change: the lead dancer at the front is now the person in [Image 1].

Use the adult in [Image 1] as the identity of the central lead dancer in a 15-second group dance video. Preserve [Video 1]'s full-body choreography, ensemble formation, warm stage lighting, camera rhythm, and fire accents. Keep the face, hair, and body proportions consistent through turns and arm movements. Do not replace the background dancers or change the stage layout.

[Image 1] replaces the lead man at the front of the stage (white T-shirt, light-blue jeans, a grey cap), in EVERY shot: copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles). They wear the clothes from [Image 1]. NO grey cap, no hat of any kind and no silver chain unless [Image 1] shows them. The lead always wears a top: never shirtless, never a bare chest; if [Image 1] shows no top, a plain white T-shirt. The same real person from the first second to the last, so their friends recognize them at once: they stay exactly the same in every second from the first frame to the last, through every zoom, blackout, spotlight, colour change of the stage light and flame burst. Never morph, never drift back to the original lead's face.

The backup dancers stay exactly as in the video, with their own faces, jackets and moves.

Shots, matching the reference second by second:
0-1.5 s: wide shot from the crowd: the lead walks out of the line of backup dancers to the front of the stage, the LED wall lights up behind.
1.5-3 s: the camera zooms in: the lead alone at the front in a white spotlight, a bouncy step on the beat.
3-5 s: the lead dances in front of the line, knees bent in a low wide stance, arms swinging; a flame column shoots up at the edge of the stage.
5-10 s: the backup dancers in a line behind the lead dance the same routine in sync, shoulder bounces, side steps and arm rolls; flame columns burst at the front of the stage.
10-12 s: a big flame in front of the lead, then the LED wall flashes, cool white light.
12-15 s: the whole line moves forward with the lead in the middle, a low crouch and a bounce, flames burst above the stage.

One head per person, on that person's own shoulders. Exactly one lead at the front. The LED wall stays exactly as in the video. No captions or subtitles, no added text, no logos, no watermark.
